title: Tech Note: Implementing OAuth2 in 4D
author: Erick Lui, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: The manual OAuth2 authorization-code-flow implementation shown here (parsing client_secrets.json, building the auth URL by hand, exchanging codes for tokens via raw HTTP POSTs) is still functionally correct, but 4D has since added first-class OAuth2 support directly into SMTP New transporter's parameters, making much of this hand-rolled plumbing unnecessary for the specific mail use case the note leads with.
related_updates: Later 4D versions added a dedicated authenticationMode: SMTP authentication OAUTH2 parameter path (already previewed at the end of this very note) that simplifies Gmail/Office365 OAuth2 mail auth considerably

For general-purpose OAuth2 (non-mail APIs), this note's manual flow using HTTP Request, JSON Parse, and ORDA-based token storage remains a valid, still-current pattern with no built-in 4D command replacing it
